classification.difficultyReason: Carry forward the shared elapsed interval, compute each distance then add the approach distances; familiar source-taught constant speed method.

content.prompt: Jill and Sophie both leave home at 8:25 a.m. and walk to school. Jill walks at a speed of 75 m/min and Sophie takes her time and walks at 60 m/min. They meet at school at 8:40 a.m.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How far does each girl live from the school?

answer.worked: Both walk for $15\text{ min}$, from 8:25 to 8:40. Jill walks $75\times15=1125\text{ m}$; Sophie walks $60\times15=900\text{ m}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Suppose Jill and Sophie start at two points on the same road and walk towards each other at the above speed and from the same times. How far apart are the points?

answer.worked: The phrase “from the same times” carries forward the same 8:25 start and 8:40 meeting time. Over those $15\text{ min}$, their closing speed is $75+60=135\text{ m/min}$. Therefore the initial separation is $135\times15=2025\text{ m}$, also $1125+900\text{ m}$.
